annotation.kind: source selection and faithful formalization of the centered-error probability bound in equation (4.12)

assumptions: The exact sum is nonzero, which makes the sum of the input magnitudes positive.
The output precision p and random-bit count r are positive.

The m rounded additions form the paper's left-to-right SR_(p,r) execution, with delta and beta linked to each actual pre-rounding value and satisfying the local error, history, conditional-mean, and zero-result requirements.
The errors alpha_k=delta_k-beta_k are mean independent and bounded by u_p, as proved in Lemma 3.10.
The centered suffix-product covariances satisfy the uniform gamma_m(u_p^2) consequence of reference [11, Lemma 3.1], which Theorem 4.3 explicitly invokes.
The corresponding second-moment inequality for M is supplied explicitly as the variance premise used to derive equation (4.12).

conditions.L: The identical fixed statement and P17 shared files are present; the frozen NumStability library is also present.
conditions.N: The fixed statement and P17 shared files are present; no NumStability artifact is present.

formal_statement.lean_header: theorem p17_t1_centered_error_probability_bound {m : Nat} {Omega : Type} [Fintype Omega] (run : P17VarianceRecursiveSumRun m Omega) (hsum : p17ExactSum run.a != 0) (hsecond : p17Expectation run.probability (fun omega => (p17CenteredSummationError run.toP17LimitedPrecisionRecursiveSumRun omega)^2) <= (sum_i abs (run.a i))^2 * p17Gamma m ((p17UnitRoundoff run.p)^2)) (lambda : Real) (hlambda_pos : 0 < lambda) (hlambda_lt_one : lambda < 1) : 1-lambda <= p17EventProb run.probability {omega | abs (p17CenteredSummationError run.toP17LimitedPrecisionRecursiveSumRun omega) <= (sum_i abs (run.a i)) * sqrt (p17Gamma m ((p17UnitRoundoff run.p)^2) / lambda)}
formal_statement.plain_language: Equation (4.12): from the stated second-moment bound, the centered recursive-summation error M lies within its variance radius with probability at least one minus lambda.

informal_proof: Use the supplied second-moment inequality for the centered term M and apply the Bienayme-Chebyshev inequality at radius (sum_i |a_i|) sqrt(gamma_m(u_p^2)/lambda). Algebra reduces the normalized second moment to lambda, yielding equation (4.12).
informal_statement: The centered-error probability estimate explicitly numbered (4.12) in the proof of Theorem 4.3.
paper_version: published journal version; SIAM Journal on Scientific Computing 47(5), 2025, pages B1227-B1249

review_record_not_for_run_prompt.note: The mounted finite Chebyshev theorem is the one substantial result. It turns the paper-invoked second-moment premise into equation (4.12); the remaining work is representation and scalar algebra.
